esp32-devkit-v1.name: ESP32 DevKit V1 / ESP32-DevKitC V4 (30-pin / 38-pin)
esp32-devkit-v1.operatingVoltage: 5V via USB or VIN (onboard 3.3V AMS1117 regulator)
esp32-devkit-v1.pins: 30–38 pins: I2C (GPIO21 SDA, GPIO22 SCL), SPI (GPIO18/19/23/5), UART2 (GPIO16/17), ADC1 (GPIO32–39 safe with Wi-Fi)
esp32-devkit-v1.current: 80–240 mA active Wi-Fi; max 12 mA recommended per GPIO (40 mA absolute max)
esp32-devkit-v1.protocol: Wi-Fi 802.11 b/g/n, Bluetooth/BLE, ESP-NOW, I2C, SPI, UART, PWM, ADC
esp32-devkit-v1.howItWorks: Dual-core 32-bit Xtensa LX6 MCU running up to 240 MHz with integrated wireless radio and hardware peripherals.
esp32-devkit-v1.precautions: Never apply 5V directly to any GPIO pin. Use ADC1 pins (GPIO32–39) when Wi-Fi is active because ADC2 is shared with Wi-Fi. Avoid strapping pins (GPIO0, GPIO2, GPIO12, GPIO15) for sensors that hold high/low at boot.

photo.credit: Espressif Systems: ESP32-DevKitC V4 Official Documentation

esp32-cam.name: ESP32-CAM (AI-Thinker Module with OV2640 Camera + FTDI Programmer)
esp32-cam.operatingVoltage: 5V regulated (minimum 500 mA–1 A peak during Wi-Fi + camera capture)
esp32-cam.pins: Limited free GPIOs (GPIO12–15 shared with microSD; GPIO0 must be shorted to GND during flashing)
esp32-cam.current: 180–350 mA average, spikes >500 mA during flash LED / Wi-Fi stream
esp32-cam.protocol: Wi-Fi, UART (via external 3.3V FTDI USB-to-Serial adapter), DVP camera bus
esp32-cam.howItWorks: ESP32-S module paired with an OV2640 2MP camera and microSD slot; requires external USB-UART programmer because it has no onboard USB port.
esp32-cam.precautions: Brownout detector triggers constantly on weak USB power, power from a solid 5V 2A supply. Always disconnect GPIO0 from GND after flashing and press RESET.

photo.credit: Conceptual visual (verify AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM pinout before wiring)

arduino-uno-r3.name: Arduino Uno R3 (ATmega328P)
arduino-uno-r3.operatingVoltage: 5V via USB or 7–12V DC barrel jack/VIN
arduino-uno-r3.pins: 14 Digital I/O (6 PWM: D3, D5, D6, D9, D10, D11), 6 Analog (A0–A5; A4=SDA, A5=SCL)
arduino-uno-r3.current: 40–50 mA board idle; max 20 mA recommended per I/O pin (40 mA absolute max)
arduino-uno-r3.protocol: UART, I2C, SPI, 10-bit ADC, PWM (no built-in Wi-Fi/BLE)
arduino-uno-r3.howItWorks: 8-bit AVR ATmega328P microcontroller at 16 MHz; ideal for deterministic local sensor/actuator control.
arduino-uno-r3.precautions: Never power motors, pumps, or servos directly from the 5V pin. Use 3.3V level shifting when connecting 3.3V-only modules.

photo.credit: Arduino Official Store: Arduino Uno R3

mpu6050.name: MPU6050 6-Axis Accelerometer & Gyroscope Module (GY-521)
mpu6050.pins: VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, XDA, XCL, AD0 (sets I2C address 0x68/0x69), INT
mpu6050.howItWorks: MEMS 3-axis accelerometer measures linear acceleration/gravity/tilt and 3-axis gyroscope measures angular velocity.
mpu6050.precautions: Connect AD0 to GND for 0x68 and to 3.3V for 0x69 when using two sensors on one I2C bus (3+ sensors need a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer).

hc-sr04.name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor (or JSN-SR04T Waterproof)
hc-sr04.logicVoltage: 5V ECHO output: MUST use 1kΩ / 2kΩ voltage divider to 3.3V on ESP32!
hc-sr04.howItWorks: Emits 40 kHz ultrasonic burst on TRIG and outputs a HIGH pulse on ECHO proportional to round-trip sound travel time.
hc-sr04.precautions: CRITICAL: Standard HC-SR04 outputs 5V on ECHO. Always drop ECHO to ~3.3V using a 1kΩ + 2kΩ resistor divider before connecting to ESP32 GPIO.

dht22.name: DHT22 (AM2302) Digital Temperature & Humidity Sensor
dht22.pins: VCC, DATA (needs 4.7kΩ–10kΩ pull-up resistor if bare sensor), GND
dht22.protocol: Single-wire proprietary digital bus (max 0.5 Hz / once every 2 seconds)
dht22.howItWorks: Measures relative humidity via capacitive element and temperature via thermistor, outputting calibrated 16-bit digital readings.
dht22.precautions: Do not poll faster than once every 2 seconds or readings return NaN.

bme280.name: BME280 / BMP280 Temperature, Humidity & Barometric Pressure Sensor
bme280.operatingVoltage: 3.3V (most breakouts are 3.3V ONLY; check regulator before 5V)
bme280.pins: VCC, GND, SCL, SDA (I2C address 0x76 or 0x77)
bme280.howItWorks: High-accuracy MEMS barometric pressure, humidity (BME280), and temperature sensor.
bme280.precautions: Verify whether your breakout is BME280 (includes humidity) vs BMP280 (no humidity) and confirm 0x76 vs 0x77 with an I2C scanner.

mq-gas.name: MQ-Series Gas/Smoke Sensor Module (MQ-2 / MQ-135 / MQ-7)
mq-gas.operatingVoltage: 5V DC required for internal SnO2 heater coil
mq-gas.logicVoltage: Up to 5V Analog Out (AO): MUST use voltage divider before ESP32 3.3V ADC!
mq-gas.pins: VCC (5V), GND, DO (digital comparator), AO (analog voltage)
mq-gas.current: 150–180 mA heater current (runs warm during operation)
mq-gas.howItWorks: Heated tin-dioxide sensing element changes electrical resistance in presence of target gases/smoke.
mq-gas.precautions: Requires 2–5 min warm-up for stable demo readings (24–48 hr burn-in for lab calibration). Not a certified life-safety gas detector. Always use a 1kΩ/2kΩ voltage divider on AO for ESP32.

pms5003.name: PMS5003 Laser PM2.5 / PM10 Particulate Matter Sensor
pms5003.operatingVoltage: 5V DC for internal fan & laser diode
pms5003.pins: PIN1 VCC (5V), PIN2 GND, PIN4 RXD, PIN5 TXD (connect sensor TXD -> ESP32 GPIO16 RX2)
pms5003.howItWorks: Internal fan draws air past a laser beam; photodiode measures light scattering to calculate PM1.0, PM2.5, and PM10 in µg/m³.
pms5003.precautions: Do not obstruct air intake/exhaust vents. Needs 30 seconds of fan spin-up for stable readings.

soil-moisture.name: Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor v1.2 / v2.0
soil-moisture.pins: VCC, GND, AOUT (connect to ESP32 ADC1 pin e.g. GPIO34)
soil-moisture.protocol: Analog ADC (higher voltage = drier, lower voltage = wetter)
soil-moisture.howItWorks: Measures dielectric permittivity of surrounding soil without exposed copper electrolysis corrosion.
soil-moisture.precautions: Coat top PCB electronics edge with conformal coating/silicone if used outdoors; calibrate DRY (air) and WET (water) ADC values before setting thresholds.

oled-096.name: 0.96-inch I2C OLED Display (SSD1306, 128×64)
oled-096.pins: GND, VCC, SCL (GPIO22 / A5), SDA (GPIO21 / A4)
oled-096.howItWorks: Self-emissive monochrome OLED matrix driven by SSD1306 controller over 2-wire I2C.
oled-096.precautions: Double-check VCC/GND pin order on your specific breakout, some modules swap pins 1 and 2.

lcd-1602-i2c.name: 16×2 Character LCD with PCF8574 I2C Backpack
lcd-1602-i2c.logicVoltage: 5V I2C (use logic level shifter or 3.3V pull-ups with ESP32)
lcd-1602-i2c.pins: GND, VCC (5V), SDA, SCL (I2C address 0x27 or 0x3F)
lcd-1602-i2c.howItWorks: Displays 2 rows × 16 ASCII characters via PCF8574 I2C expander.
lcd-1602-i2c.precautions: Adjust blue potentiometer on the back if screen shows blank or solid blocks.

relay-module.name: Optocoupled Relay Module (5V or 3.3V Trigger) / Logic-Level MOSFET
relay-module.operatingVoltage: 5V DC coil supply (separate from MCU if driving multiple channels)
relay-module.pins: VCC, GND, IN (control), COM, NO (Normally Open), NC (Normally Closed)
relay-module.howItWorks: Electromagnetically switches a higher-current isolated DC load (pump, fan, lamp) using a tiny microcontroller signal.
relay-module.precautions: Prefer 5V–12V DC loads for student builds. NEVER wire mains AC without qualified adult supervision, fused enclosure, and proper insulation. Add a 1N4007 flyback diode across inductive DC pumps/motors.

servo-motor.name: Servo Motor (SG90 Micro / MG996R High-Torque)
servo-motor.operatingVoltage: 4.8V–6.0V External DC Supply (NEVER power MG996R from ESP32 3.3V/USB!)
servo-motor.logicVoltage: 3.3V–5V PWM control signal (50 Hz, 1–2 ms pulse)
servo-motor.pins: Brown/Black = GND (common with MCU), Red = +5V External, Orange/Yellow = PWM Signal
servo-motor.current: SG90: 250–500 mA stall; MG996R: 1.2–2.5 A stall
servo-motor.howItWorks: Closed-loop geared DC motor with internal potentiometer that holds a commanded angle (0°–180°).
servo-motor.precautions: Power servos from a dedicated 5V 2A+ external supply and tie external GND to MCU GND to prevent brownout resets.

l298n-driver.name: L298N / TB6612FNG Dual H-Bridge Motor Driver
l298n-driver.pins: 12V/VM, GND (common with MCU), IN1–IN4, ENA/ENB, OUT1–OUT4
l298n-driver.current: Up to 2 A per channel (L298N drops ~2V; TB6612FNG is more efficient)
l298n-driver.howItWorks: H-bridge transistor array reverses polarity and modulates PWM duty cycle to control DC motor speed and direction.
l298n-driver.precautions: NEVER connect DC motors directly to microcontroller GPIO pins. Always connect motor battery GND to microcontroller GND.

dc-pump.name: 5V–12V Submersible Mini DC Water Pump
dc-pump.operatingVoltage: 5V–12V External DC Supply (switched via Relay or MOSFET)
dc-pump.logicVoltage: Driven via Relay / N-channel MOSFET (NOT direct GPIO)
dc-pump.pins: Red (+V via relay NO / MOSFET drain), Black (GND)
dc-pump.current: 200–600 mA running (up to 1 A startup surge)
dc-pump.howItWorks: Centrifugal impeller pushes water through silicone tubing when energized.
dc-pump.precautions: Never run submersible pump dry for extended periods. Add a 1N4007 flyback diode across pump terminals and keep water strictly separated from electronics.

gps-neo6m.name: NEO-6M GPS Receiver Module with Ceramic Antenna
gps-neo6m.pins: VCC, GND, TX (to ESP32 RX2 GPIO16), RX (to ESP32 TX2 GPIO17)
gps-neo6m.howItWorks: Receives L1 GPS satellite timing signals to calculate latitude, longitude, altitude, and UTC time.
gps-neo6m.precautions: Requires clear view of sky (outdoors or near window) for first cold satellite fix (30–120 seconds).

tp4056-solar.name: TP4056 Li-Ion Charger (with DW01A Protection) + 18650 Cell + 5V Solar Panel
tp4056-solar.operatingVoltage: 5V solar/USB input -> 4.2V charge termination on 3.7V Li-Ion cell
tp4056-solar.logicVoltage: Power rail only (boost/buck to stable 5V or 3.3V LDO for MCU)
tp4056-solar.pins: IN+/IN- (5V solar/USB), B+/B- (18650 cell), OUT+/OUT- (protected load output)
tp4056-solar.current: Up to 1 A charge (adjust Rprog resistor for small solar panels)
tp4056-solar.howItWorks: Charges single-cell 3.7V lithium-ion battery using CC/CV profile with over-discharge/short protection.
tp4056-solar.precautions: Use ONLY protected 18650 cells or protected TP4056 boards (with OUT+/OUT-). Never short-circuit or puncture Li-Ion cells. Do not leave charging unattended near flammable materials.

ad8232-max30102.name: AD8232 Single-Lead ECG Module / MAX30102 Pulse Oximeter
ad8232-max30102.pins: AD8232: 3.3V, GND, OUTPUT (GPIO34), LO+, LO-; MAX30102: VIN (3.3V), GND, SDA, SCL
ad8232-max30102.howItWorks: Amplifies tiny biopotential voltage differences (AD8232) or optical photoplethysmography pulse absorption (MAX30102).
ad8232-max30102.precautions: EDUCATIONAL PROTOTYPE ONLY: NOT A MEDICAL DEVICE. CRITICAL SAFETY: When using AD8232 skin electrodes, ALWAYS power the ESP32 from an isolated battery/power bank, NEVER from a mains-connected laptop or wall charger!

passive-alert-kit.name: Active Buzzer, LEDs (R/Y/G), 220Ω Resistors, Push Buttons, Breadboard & Jumpers
passive-alert-kit.logicVoltage: Digital GPIO (with 220Ω current-limiting resistor per LED)
passive-alert-kit.pins: LED Anode (+) -> 220Ω -> GPIO, Cathode (-) -> GND; Button -> GPIO (INPUT_PULLUP) + GND
passive-alert-kit.current: 5–15 mA per LED; 15–30 mA active buzzer
passive-alert-kit.howItWorks: Provides immediate local visual/audio feedback and manual override/reset controls.
passive-alert-kit.precautions: Always place a 220Ω–330Ω resistor in series with every LED to protect both the LED and the microcontroller GPIO pin.
